HM01-q01-2oab10: The "H" endorsement is needed for a HazMat vehicle of any size, not only combination vehicles.
It is not limited to tankers; a vehicle of any size hauling HazMat needs the "H" endorsement.
HM01-q02-erl8nu: A CLP holder is prohibited from hauling HazMat, even with a licensed driver on board.
There is no in-state exception; a CLP holder may not haul HazMat anywhere.
HM01-q03-pgfr2k: 1 year is a carrier's copy-keeping time; HazMat training and testing is at least once every 3 years.
2 years is how long shippers keep shipping papers; training and testing is at least once every 3 years.
HM01-q04-mn3m5u: Labels, papers, emergency response information and placards communicate the risk; packaging contains the material.
Assuring safe drivers and equipment is the knowledge-test goal; packaging rules are containment rules.
HM01-q05-su7y6u: The carrier checks the shipper's work and refuses improper loads; the shipper packages, labels and supplies placards.
The driver checks the load and placards at loading; the shipper packages, labels, writes the papers and supplies placards.
HM01-q06-lelh0q: Refusing leaking packages and shipments is one of the driver's duties.
Placarding the vehicle when loading, if required, is one of the driver's duties.
HM01-q07-p96cex: The carrier must check the shipment before transporting it, not after delivery.
The carrier checks every HazMat shipment before moving it, placarded or not, and refuses improper ones.
HM01-q08-nuxi0p: 6 is the number of Column 1 symbols in the table; there are 9 hazard classes.
4 is the minimum number of placards on a placarded vehicle; there are 9 hazard classes.
HM01-q09-6o3eyd: Never hide HazMat papers; keep them on top or clearly marked, in the door pouch or in clear view within reach.
The sleeper berth is not within immediate reach; use the door pouch or clear view within reach while belted.
HM01-q10-83p3vm: Responders must find the papers fast; when you leave the vehicle, put them on the driver's seat.
Locked papers can't be found fast; when you are out of the vehicle, leave them on the driver's seat.
HM01-q11-zkvqy1: The package still needs its label; if it won't fit, the shipper uses a securely attached tag.
If a label won't fit, the shipper puts it on a tag attached to the package; cylinders get tags or decals.
HM01-q12-ssapxd: No permit makes it legal; never transport a material marked "Forbidden".
Placards don't make it legal; never transport a material marked "Forbidden".
HM01-q13-10jwvl: The material's hazard class is one of the 3 facts needed to choose placards.
The total amount of all HazMat of all classes on the vehicle is one of the 3 facts.
HM01-q14-jxblw0: G means a generic shipping name, not a gas; a technical name must follow it on the shipping paper.
Air-only is symbol A; G is a generic name that needs a technical name added.
HM01-q15-3ycrj6: "UN" is used in front of ID numbers.
"NA" is used in front of ID numbers for names used only in the U.S. and to/from Canada.
HM01-q16-blfda6: Marine pollutants are listed in Appendix B; Column 7 numbers 1–6 mean poison inhalation hazard.
Packing groups are in Column 5, in Roman numerals; Column 7 numbers 1–6 mean poison inhalation hazard.
HM01-q17-ywruhv: Column 7 (special provisions) and Column 8 (packaging) apply; only Columns 9 and 10 don't apply to highway.
Column 1 symbols and Column 2 shipping names apply to highway; Columns 9 and 10 do not.
HM01-q18-gxflsr: RQ means reportable quantity, not a route restriction; spills of that amount must be reported.
Water-only is the Column 1 symbol W; RQ means reportable quantity.
HM01-q19-aok50a: INHALATION HAZARD needs POISON INHALATION HAZARD or POISON GAS placards even for small amounts.
Class placards alone are not enough; add POISON INHALATION HAZARD or POISON GAS placards, even for small amounts.
HM01-q20-ekc85w: The MARINE POLLUTANT sign is a marking, not a placard, and it does not replace class placards.
Highway bulk packages of marine pollutants show the marking, also on the outside of the vehicle.
HM01-q21-4k1u0r: The ID number comes first: ID number, proper shipping name, hazard class, packing group.
Hazard class comes third; the order is ID number, proper shipping name, hazard class, packing group.
HM01-q22-u94704: Entering the HazMat first is one of the allowed ways to show it.
An "X" (or "RQ") in the HM column is one of the allowed ways to show it.
HM01-q23-pqgac9: The first page must show the total number of pages; the shipper, not the driver, signs the certification.
The first page must show the total number of pages, such as "Page 1 of 3".
HM01-q24-vnsslv: The emergency response phone number is the shipper's responsibility, not the driver's.
The consignee receives the load; the shipper provides the emergency response phone number.
HM01-q25-3qgy3v: Immediate hazards to health are part of the minimum emergency response information.
Basic first aid steps are part of the minimum emergency response information.
HM01-q26-07qone: 1 year is the carrier's copy in the carrier-service-only case; shippers keep hazardous waste papers 3 years.
2 years is for other HazMat; shippers keep hazardous waste papers 3 years.
HM01-q27-mbpoj9: Not knowing a product is a reason to ask the shipper to contact your office, not to refuse the certification.
Crossing a state line doesn't matter; refuse only if a package is clearly unsafe or doesn't follow the HMR.
